packageRules.description: dtolnay/rust-toolchain's @stable/@beta/@nightly refs are branch names in that action's own repo that intentionally track the current toolchain -- SHA-pinning them (helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests' default) freezes CI on whatever commit happened to be HEAD at pin time instead of tracking new Rust releases.

bincode 3.0.0 is a placeholder/reserved release, not a real major version -- its published source is a single `compile_error!("https://xkcd.com/2347/")` and it has zero dependencies (confirmed 2026-09-25 by checking out the crate directly from crates.io). Block that specific version; a legitimate future 2.x or working 3.x release is still allowed.

wgpu and eframe/egui/egui-wgpu must move together in crates/nicti-tapetum and crates/nicti-pelt -- eframe/egui-wgpu pin an exact wgpu version internally (ADR-0068's Hard gate 2), so a wgpu-only bump landing without a matching eframe/egui-wgpu bump (or vice versa) would silently split the workspace onto two incompatible wgpu type sets, the same failure class the now-deleted spikes/pelt-iced/wgpu-27 pin (#232) existed to avoid.

spikes/* are throwaway research crates deleted on promotion (see CLAUDE.md's package map section) -- a bump PR against one is pure churn nobody will act on before the whole crate is deleted or promoted. A dependency shared with a real crates/* or root manifest still gets bumped normally via that manifest's own PR. (spikes/den, this rule's original motivating case with its five already-rejected catalog-engine candidates, was itself deleted in #123.)
